skill.name: agent-memory-mcp
skill.description: Provides an MCP-based memory bank for searchable AI agent project knowledge, decisions, patterns, and notes.
skill.summary: Connect AI agents to persistent project memory through an MCP server.
skill.author: Amit Rathiesh

security_audit.summary: The SKILL.md file mainly contains Markdown setup and MCP tool usage documentation, so many backtick detections are false positives. Real risk remains because the skill instructs users to clone an unpinned third-party repository, run npm install and compile commands, and start local MCP and dashboard processes. No prompt injection language was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the cloned repository to a reviewed commit or release and document an integrity verification step.
Use a reviewed lockfile and document whether install scripts are required before running npm install.

remediation.issue: Local MCP server and dashboard startup
remediation.suggestion: Document bind address, data directory, permissions, and shutdown steps for the server and dashboard.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger static risk
remediation.suggestion: Separate manual setup commands from inline MCP tool examples and mark them as user-reviewed commands.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 uses Markdown inline code for the project name only. It does not invoke Ruby backticks or execute a shell command.

Line 30 is the closing Markdown fence after the install block. It does not itself execute a command or define command substitution.
The range includes npm run start-server with a project id and workspace path. Starting an MCP server from cloned code is a real runtime command risk.
The cited text is Markdown fence and example-introduction text. The executable example appears on a later separately reported line.
The range includes the concrete start-server example with shell expansion of the current directory. It is documentation, but it directs command execution for the MCP server.
Line 43 closes a Markdown code block before the capabilities section. It is not Ruby backtick execution.
Line 47 is a Markdown heading with the memory_search tool name in inline code. It documents an MCP tool and does not invoke a shell.
Line 51 lists argument names in Markdown inline code. These are schema-like labels, not executable shell or Ruby syntax.
Line 52 shows an MCP tool usage example in inline code. It is not a shell command and is not executed by the Markdown file.
Line 54 is a Markdown heading with the memory_write tool name. It documents a tool name rather than executing code.
Line 58 lists memory_write argument names in inline code. This is documentation, not a shell execution pattern.
Line 59 contains an illustrative MCP memory_write call. It is not shell syntax and does not run automatically.
Line 61 is a Markdown heading with an inline MCP tool name. It does not perform Ruby or shell execution.
Line 65 documents a single argument name in inline code. There is no executable command at this location.
Line 66 shows an MCP memory_read usage example. It is not shell syntax and does not execute from the skill file.
Line 68 is a Markdown heading with an inline MCP tool name. It is documentation only.
Line 72 documents a memory_stats tool call example. It is not a shell command and is not automatically executed.
The cited dashboard block includes npm run start-dashboard with a workspace path argument. Running a dashboard process from cloned code is a real local execution risk.
Line 80 closes the dashboard Markdown block. The following localhost URL is an access note, not shell or Ruby execution.
The command substitution only runs pwd, but it is part of an npm server startup command intended for workspace execution. This is a limited command-execution concern.
The detector appears to interpret a Markdown bash fence as a template literal. The real shell command is covered by the separate line 42 finding.
The setup fetches code from a GitHub URL without pinning a commit or release. This creates supply-chain risk if the external repository changes.
The URL points to localhost for the dashboard after local startup. It does not indicate external network egress or a remote service dependency.
The description says the skill provides searchable knowledge management for AI agents. It does not instruct system enumeration or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: AI agents often lose project context between sessions. This skill connects them to an MCP memory bank for searchable decisions, patterns, and notes.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup of the agentMemory MCP server from a GitHub repository.
Searches stored memories by query, type, and tags.
Writes project knowledge with a key, type, content, and optional tags.
Reads a specific memory entry by key.
Starts a local dashboard for viewing memory usage.
limitations: Requires cloning and running a separate external project.
Only retrieves knowledge that was previously written to memory.
Security depends on the reviewed state of the cloned repository and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Resume Project Work
use_cases.description: Recover prior architecture decisions and implementation patterns before editing a project.

use_cases.title: Share Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Store project decisions so future agents and teammates can find the same context.

use_cases.title: Review Repeated Patterns
use_cases.description: Search memory for recurring design choices before changing authentication, deployment, or data flows.

prompt_templates.title: Search Existing Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a simple lookup before planning work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use memory_search to find project decisions about authentication. Summarize the relevant entries with source keys.

prompt_templates.title: Save a Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Record a new project choice after discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use memory_write to save the decision to use token rotation. Include the reason, tradeoffs, and tags for authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Known Entry
prompt_templates.scenario: Retrieve one stored memory before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use memory_read to retrieve the deployment-pipeline decision. Compare it with the current implementation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Memory Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit memory quality before a large project change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use memory_stats and targeted searches to identify stale or missing architecture memories for this project.

output_examples.input: Find all authentication patterns in project memory.
output_examples.output: The response lists matching memory entries, their keys, and short summaries of the stored authentication guidance.

output_examples.input: Save this architecture decision about token rotation.
output_examples.output: The decision is stored with a clear key, decision type, concise content, and authentication tags.

output_examples.input: Show memory statistics for this workspace.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes memory counts, available types, and recent usage signals from the memory bank.

best_practices: Pin and review the external agentMemory repository before installing it.
Use stable memory keys and consistent tags for repeatable searches.
Avoid storing secrets, credentials, or sensitive personal data in memory.
anti_patterns: Do not run setup commands in an untrusted workspace without review.
Do not store raw API keys, access tokens, or private customer data.
Do not treat memory entries as source of truth without checking current files.

faq.question: What does this skill add to an AI assistant?
faq.answer: It adds access to a persistent MCP memory bank for project decisions, patterns, notes, and statistics.

faq.question: Does it work without Node.js?
faq.answer: No. The documented setup requires Node.js version 18 or newer.

faq.question: Can it search old project decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search stored memories by query, type, and tags.

faq.question: Can it write new memory entries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can save knowledge with a key, type, content, and optional tags.

faq.question: Does it include a dashboard?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation describes a local dashboard available on port 3333.

faq.question: What should users review before setup?
faq.answer: Users should review the cloned repository, package scripts, and dependency lock state before running install commands.
